Can I tell you orally since the witness is not listening to this. The witness said: "I learned later," if that is of any value to you, "that five or six shells landed on ..." et cetera. So, in other words the witness qualified this by saying these were not his personal observations and perhaps if we could clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness -- Ms. Mahindaratne, I take it that you will give that some follow up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness put on his earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic, you testified that there were also five or six shells that landed on the high school building which was in the immediate vicinity of the football pitch. Now, was that based on your own observations, or did you learn about it through another source?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: If you listened carefully, I said that I learned of this later at the time when I was not in Benkovac; in other words, in the period when I was in Obrovac. I did not personally see those shells landing there, nor did I hear them. Rather, later on, I was told of this by someone, that the football pitch of the high school was hit and also the gym. I didn't have time -- at the time I didn't have time to go and check whether this was true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you say that you learned of it when you were in Obrovac. Did you learn of this particular shelling of the high school on the 4th itself?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] When did you learn of it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at some point after I returned from Obrovac, let's say around noon or around 1.00 p.m. I heard this from the police station employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you learned of it on the 4th August itself, that day itself. That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on the 4th of August. That was when I was in Benkovac. I was there the whole day. I also went there on the 5th, but early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you went there on the 5th, did you observe any damage that was consistent with this information?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not inspect this on the 5th, because, as early as 7.30 on the 5th, I left Benkovac, and during the night, I had some other responsibilities that had to do with evacuating certain documents and equipment from the police station. So that I did not have time to go and check those places that were mentioned, and as I said, I only heard of this from the employees the police -- who were at the police station at the time. So all of this was happening while I was away from Benkovac, when I was in Obrovac, on the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vukasinovic, just one last question. At paragraphs 10 and 11, you referred to returning to Benkovac at 10.30; that is, after going to Obrovac, and being present at the police station from that point onwards till 5.00 p.m. Now between 10.30 and approximately 5.00, are you able to say about how many shells would have landed in the area you were? Now you made an assessment of 100 shells falling between, up to 7.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. If there's a question on the table, that has been asked. So if the witness could get the opportunity to answer it, as opposed to asked another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask a question, Mr. President. I was just going to clarify my question in case there was misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Ms. Mahindaratne thinks that the question will be clearer after she has further explained it, she is allowed to do so. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now you made an assessment saying between -- up to 7.00 approximately 100 shells would have landed. Now my question to you is from 10.30 to 5.00, approximately how many shells would have landed? Can you make an assessment of that nature?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me earlier, you mentioned in my immediate vicinity. Well, during that period, two shells landed on the football pitch in my immediate vicinity, and I have described this already. Now in this period the Ristici hamlet and the barracks were under fire and the facilities that I have already mentioned. Between 10.30 or 11.00 when I returned from Obrovac, up until 5.00 p.m., in my assessment, some 30 or 40 shells landed. To be honest, I did not keep count of them, but approximately in my free estimate it would be around that number. As for the two shells that I described landing on the football pitch, they fell in my immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukasinovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Kehoe, you would have further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Often this is the moment when the Chamber questions are --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may have a question, but I would first want to invite the witness to take his earphones off again. Mr. Kehoe, whether or not I have a question for the witness depends a bit on how to interpret one of the maps. Of course, we haven't got the markings here yet. They will come at a later stage. But you showed the witness the map, you remember with the yellow roads on it, the important roads. I see the Ristici. Could we have that on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's D1501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I -- Yes. There it is, although still unmarked. I think the witness said that where the shells in the pine wood fell was at 77, approximately, which is just above Benkovacko Selo, and you asked him the distance from the police station to that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you didn't ask him to tell us where the police station was but, I take it, from D248 which is the map indicated on it all kind of facilities, I would say it would be very close to what we see on this map as being depicted as 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- could be a -- 50 metres off that, but that's -- I would think it was a little bit further down from the 6 in westerly direction. But that's -- that's minimal. Now, if we look at the scale of this map, could we move the map so that we can see the scale and ... I see a scale which apparently is related to miles. Now, first of all, Mr. Kehoe, this 1573 metres, where do you start in reading this scale? To the left part of it, the -- where it's just above the DA of Datumi Slika or the next bus-stop, I would say, which is just above, between the 0 and the S for Srpanj? What is the 1573?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm speculating at this point without full knowledge. I understand now it is the entire span from left to right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if you look at that, approximately at that scale, 1573 metres, if I try to figure out what the distance between 76, to take it as a rough estimate, and 77 would be, that would not be anywhere near to 700 metres, as the crow flies. I must tell you that I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- problems in accepting that your interpretation of the scale is the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Between 76 and 77 is 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the grid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom out a tiny little bit then we -- yes. And -- but, therefore, if I look at this scale and, of course, we can measure that. If we now not change the scale anymore, that would be very helpful. If your interpretation would be right, it would be 2 kilometres. So I am wondering whether your interpretation of the scale is the correct one. I'm inclined to believe that it is the smaller portion -- or the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In these maps, Mr. President, the way they're laid out, the grid reference from the 76 to the 77 is a kilometre. If we go from the grid that's on the bottom - and I'm just eyeballing it at this point - it appears to be approximately the same. And we can -- we can actually go back and give you a map of the distance between the two. But we were giving a rough approximation with the witness without holding him to a specific locale. But these are maps obviously taken off Google Earth, and the distances between these two, I assume, are pretty well established. We can certainly go back and check this distance, Mr. President, and come up with a more accurate distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, I'm not unfamiliar with Google Earth or Google Maps, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And because as we see on this map, the distance as the crow flies would be -- if that is 1573 metres, then it would -- if the scale is correct, then it would not be as the crow flies anything near 700 metres; it would be far more. It would be up to one and a half kilometre, if not more. Because if you put the scale of 1573 metres as just explained by you over there, then I would be more inclined to believe that perhaps the full scale, not from the first to the third bus-stop, but up to and including the fifth bus-stop would 1573 metres be. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think you're absolutely right, Judge. I think the whole scale is 1500 plus metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not to halfway -- I'd say 1573.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That has been clarified. I think that I have got no further questions then for the witness. It just appears in the middle and whether that covers up till there or the whole of it is not entirely clear. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, having followed my exchange of views with Mr. Kehoe, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think it is it of no need to ask the witness further specifications, whether it was 700 metres or 1.000 metres, or that's all within the normal limit of -- of error. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Some more questions will be put to you, Mr. Vukasinovic, by Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic on page 45, line 11 and 12, you noted that the Benkovac factory was -- I'll read to you exactly what you said: "Bagat was not the branch unit of the Bagat factory in Zadar -- was the branch unit of the Bagat factory in Zadar, was not fitted out nor for the production of any equipment or armaments. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.text: It does not refer to the factory but to the barracks. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you for that clarification. Now, with regard to some of the evacuation questions asked by Ms. Mahindaratne, let me show you D932.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, that's at tab 17.

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: Even if I did participate in drafting plans such as these, that would renature only to traffic control; in other words, to ensure that there was a normal flow of people and vehicles, and I didn't know anything about fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you another document from the Ministry of the Interior for the Republic of Serbian Krajina, D253. And as a preface to route -- and that's at, if I may, tab 11, Mr. Registrar. As a preface to this, in response to some questions by Ms. Mahindaratne, you noted that the evacuation was not meant to be permanent but just temporary. I show you this document, and if you could take a look at this document that's in front of you, it reflects the evacuation -- well, says -- let me read it very briefly, just the preface: "Due to the declaration of a state of war in the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina" -- I'm sorry, it's D254. I'm sorry if I -- did I say D253?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's D254; my apologies. But it's still tab 11, Mr. Registrar, in your -- Mr. Mr. Vukasinovic's book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is dated 31 July 1995. Enlisted in the first item, birth certificates, weapons registries, vehicle files. In 2, personnel -- employee personnel documents, records of the -- of the dead and wounded. And it's -- you can review this document. It goes into any number of specific items that call to be evacuated, and it's signed by Toso Pajic. Now, you know Mr. Pajic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: Not personally, no. Only by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You know who he is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: He was one of the chiefs, as indicated by his signature, the heading says the office of the minister. So he was something in the office of the minister of the interior. But what he -- I did not know him personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Vukasinovic, did you see this order after it was issued on the 31st of July, 1995, calling for the evacuation of all of this documentation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- could we have a look at the top of this document before --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I misspoke on the document, so it is D254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, no, I'd rather go to the first page again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You described the order as an order to evacuate these documents, whereas the beginning of the document says that one should be prepared for it. And at the end of it, it says who decides whether or not to evacuate these documents. So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- have I doubts as to whether this is a proper --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. President. Let me clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, and put the question in such a way to the witness that it is reflecting accurately the order. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic, my question to you with regard to these documents was not precise enough, and that was my fault. I ask you, were you aware of this order by Mr. Pajic that was written on the 31st of July, calling for the preparation to evacuate these documents? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this order, so I was not aware of the existence of such an order. And apart from that, that was not within my line of duty in my -- at my post in the police station at Benkovac. I suppose that it existed at the time as it addressed as it was to all the secretariats and the organisation of units. But, as for me, this is the first time that I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On that same score, if I could just ask you about one other document which was dated the 2nd of August, and this will be at tab 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, this is it at D938. D938. Again, this is an another preparatory document, Mr. President, not the actual evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if you can take a look at this document, again tab 20 in the book, this is a document from the 2nd of August, again, calling for the preparation of the evacuation, preparations for evacuation of material, cultural, and other assets. utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic, you noted during your direct examination and both in cross that there was no need to issue an evacuation order -- there was no need to issue the evacuation order because people were in panic. That is in the substance of your testimony. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If there was no need to issue the evacuation order, Mr. Vukasinovic, why was the order actually issued?

utterances.speaker: DJURO VUKASINOVIC
utterances.text: The order was issued at a certain time of the day; I believe it was between 1730 and 1800 hours, but the people had started fleeing much before that, because the assumption was that the Croatian army was advancing on all the parts of the front. Apart from that, shells kept falling on the area of the town of Benkovac, so that the people started fleeing prior to the formal issuance of an evacuation order. And when the people started to flee, everything -- everybody had left by the late evening hours. Benkovac was totally deserted by that time, by early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasinovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming to the video-conference room and for giving your testimony, answering the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My gratitude to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes our videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me deal with a few procedural matters before we adjourn for the day. Is the next witness -- is the next witness available already or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. It -- he will be here tomorrow. It's a prescheduled time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He will be here tomorrow, then we will use our remaining time for some procedural matters. First of all, there was an application still pending for a subpoena for the witness, I think, who just testified. The witness now testified through videolink. May I take it that this application has become moot or is withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. It is beyond moot. There is no need for the subpoena. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's now on the record that that application has been withdrawn. I move on to another matter, which always also comes perhaps a bit late. The text was ready last week, but we didn't find time to read it, and I didn't want to re-call the parties just for this purpose. But the Chamber still owes you the reasons for its decision to hear witness, then still called AG-61, Mr. Vukasinovic, via conference. These are the Chamber's reasons for its decision granting the Gotovina's Defence's motion for Witness Vukasinovic to testify via video-conference link. On the 15th of May, 2009, the Gotovina Defence applied for the issuance of a subpoena directing witnesses Vukasinovic to appear before the Chamber on 10th of June, 2009. I add to this that, at that time he was still referred to as Witness AG-61. In its application the Gotovina Defence stated that the witness refused to appear voluntarily but also mentioned that the witness had indicated a willingness to testify via video-conference link. On the 3rd of June the Gotovina Defence expressed its intention to file a separate motion for -- for this witness to testify by video-conference link, and the Prosecution announced that it had no objections. See transcript pages 17973, 974, and 18049. The Gotovina Defence subsequently filed the motion on the 4th of June. And on the 5th of June, the Prosecution, the Cermak Defence, and the Markac Defence made no objections to the motion. On the same day, the Chamber delivered its decision to grant this motion and place the Gotovina Defence request for a subpoena on hold. I refer you to transcript pages 18201 and 18202. According to Rule 81 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Chamber may order that proceedings be conducted by way of video-conference link if it is consistent with the interests of justice. This standard is met only if, first, the witness is unable or has good reasons to be unwilling to come to the seat of the Tribunal; second, the witness's testimony is sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it; and, third, the accused are not prejudiced in the exercise of their rights to confront the witness. Applying this standard, the Chamber first accepted that Witness Vukasinovic is physically unable to travel to The Hague to testify before the Tribunal. The Chamber took into consideration the fact that the witness has serious health problems. The Gotovina Defence submitted that the witness informed the victims and witness section that he suffers from angina pectoris, asthma, and a blood vessel obstruction and is awaiting to receive by-pass surgery in October or November 2009. The Chamber was informed by the Gotovina Defence on two separate occasions that confirming medical reports have been sought from the witness and will be provided shortly. I'm giving the reasons for the decision as it was given at the time. I refer you to transcript pages 17905 and 17973. Due to the urgency of the matter and the fact that none of the parties opposed the motion, the Chamber proceeded in making its decision without these reports. Ultimately, should the medical reports not corroborate the health conditions that Witness Vukasinovic claims to suffer, the parties may ask the Chamber to reconsider its decision. Second, having been apprised of the substance of the witness's anticipated testimony, the Chamber was also satisfied that the testimony of Witness Vukasinovic is sufficiently important. The Chamber deemed the importance of this testimony such that it would be unfair to require the Gotovina Defence to proceed without it. Finally, the Chamber found that neither the other accused, nor the Prosecution would be prejudiced in the exercise of their right to confront Witness Vukasinovic, if the witness were to appear via video-conference link. These parties, none of whom objected to the motion, will all be provided the opportunity to cross-examine the witness. And for these reasons and pursuant to Rule 81 bis, the Chamber granted the motion for Witness, then still referred to as Witness AG-61, to present evidence via conference link. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons on this decision. I would like to deliver a brief statement by the Chamber on scheduling. It's a statement on the further scheduling of court time in this case, for the time up to the summer recess. The Chamber already informed the parties at the Pre-Defence Conference on the 27th of May, 2009, that the courtroom schedule in this case might need to be adapted due to the fact that two Judges on this Bench are also sitting on the case against Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic. For the time being, the parties should continue to plan with five sessions per week; however, depending on the developments in the Stanisic and Simatovic case, this might be decreased to four sessions a week. Having said that, should such a reduction become necessary, the Chamber has already identified four days which potentially may be dropped from the courtroom schedule in this case. These days are: Monday, the 29th of June; Monday, the 6th of July; Thursday, the 16th of July; and Monday, the 20th of July. The Chamber will endeavour to give a more definitive decision on the scheduling matter as soon as circumstances allow for it. This concludes the Chamber's statement in this respect. I add to this, Mr. Kehoe, that you have informed the Chamber that due to other matters you have to attend, that you would prefer, if to the extent possible, not to sit on the 10th of July and the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber received this information and has considered whether, already at this time, and, of course, this is all very much provisional, whether it could meet your request, and that certainly is not possible in relation to the 10th of July. Whether there still would be a possibility not to sit on Friday, the 17th, rather than on, Thursday, the 16th, is very uncertain. Chances are small, but we will nevertheless further explore whether Thursday, the 16th of July could still be exchanged for Friday, the 17th. But as matters stand now, it is still the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.text: We have not ignored what you asked us, but just for your information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take that it if you are not present in court, that Mr. Misetic would be there anyhow. But I take it that it is because of witnesses, perhaps, that you would prefer to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On a personal level, he can't live without me, Judge. Just kidding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some people can't live without, and at the same time, not with the same. I don't know whether that is your situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm kidding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, you were kidding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just on one separate note on scheduling. I noted from the order of the Chamber concerning the hearing on the 26th of June, Your Honour had scheduled a Rule 54 hearing, I believe. And on that date I trust that we don't have to have a witness present at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider that. It depends, of course, on how much time that hearing would go take.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it might not take the whole of the day. But -- so, therefore, we will consider --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how much time it would take. If the parties would be able to assist the Chamber. It is not our intention to repeat all of the submissions, but the Chamber would have some questions, perhaps, which it would seek an answer to and that -- but we'll consider how much time that will take and then informally tell you whether we would expect other -- to hear other testimony that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then having dealt with that matter, there are a few decisions to be delivered. That is -- the first is in relation to two audio clips that were used by the Gotovina Defence. It's 1D33-0081 and 1D33-0082. The Gotovina Defence used these two audio clips during the testimony of Mr. Galbraith. The Chamber, at that time, delayed tendering a decision on admission until the Prosecution had reviewed those clips. You find that at transcript page 5065. On the 9th of June, 2009, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that it had no objection to admission. That's found on transcript page 18381. The Registrar is invited to assign exhibit numbers to the two audio clips.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D33-0081 becomes Exhibit D1502. And 1D33-0082 becomes Exhibit D1503.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1502 and D1503 are admitted into evidence. I move to the next item, which is about a video-clip known under the exhibit number D1451. It was marked at the time but not admitted during the housekeeping session on the 5th of March. The Gotovina Defence sought admission into evidence again on 8th of June of this year, and the Prosecution did not object to it. For those reasons, D1455 is admitted into evidence. Next one is D1497. It is a satellite picture on which Witness -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. I -- on line 12 of page 67, you said D1455 is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I should have said then 451 because that was -- that was what I was talking about. Yes. I apologise for the mistake. The exhibit was tendered during the witness's testimony on the 10th of June, but the Chamber forgot to state on the record that the exhibit was admitted into evidence. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would then just want to -- if I may, Mr. President, I think that's under seal because --
